title: Azure Key Vault Overview
description: Learn what Azure Key Vault does, why you should centralize secrets, and how it protects cryptographic keys.

data.text: Azure Key Vault is a cloud service for securely storing and accessing secrets. A secret can be a password, API key, certificate, or cryptographic key. Key Vault keeps these items encrypted and controls who can access them.
Key Vault also provides hardware security module (HSM) backed keys for scenarios that require FIPS 140-2 compliance.

data.title: Key Vault Objects
items: Secrets — passwords, connection strings, API keys
Keys — RSA or elliptic-curve keys for encryption and signing
Certificates — TLS/SSL or code-signing certificates with auto-renewal

rows: Key Vault SDK or REST API

data.title: Create a Key Vault with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision a new Key Vault in your resource group.
data.code: az keyvault create   --name myKeyVault   --resource-group myResourceGroup   --location eastus   --enable-soft-delete true

data.caption: How applications, Key Vault, and Entra ID work together.
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    A["Your App"] -->|"Authenticate with MI"| E["Entra ID"]
    A -->|"Get secret / key"| KV["Key Vault"]
    KV -->|"Validate token"| E
    KV -->|"Return secret"| A

data.title: Soft Delete
data.text: Always enable soft-delete on Key Vault. If someone accidentally deletes a secret, soft-delete lets you recover it within the retention period.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Key Vault stores secrets, keys, and certificates in one place.
Access is controlled by Entra ID identities and RBAC or access policies.
Soft-delete protects against accidental or malicious deletion.
data.takeaway: Move every hardcoded secret out of your code and into Key Vault.
